extracted.intended_audience: actors, comedians, and entertainment/industry readers (aspiring and professional performers)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and career-oriented guidance for performers on comedic acting, risk-taking, authenticity, hidden-camera/prank work, and navigating fame drawn from a Hollywood roundtable with veteran comedy actors. Useful for actors, stand-up comedians, and those producing edgy comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedy should be dangerous
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The panel repeatedly endorses doing risky, boundary-pushing work for laughs — from physical stunts (hoisting oneself onto a table) to provocative hidden-camera scenarios — as an artistic principle. Examples: Jim Carrey describing getting on a table and being willing to get hit; Sacha Baron Cohen recounting playing high-risk scenes with Secret Service present. Anti-pattern: playing only safe, inoffensive material that avoids stakes or consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t play it safe — take risks
rubrics_metrics.description: "I get angry at myself when I play it safe" (Ted Danson).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performers should push beyond 'adequate' choices; value boldness and escalation. Jim Carrey and others describe physical, extreme, or provocative choices that create distinctive comedy. Scoring note: higher risk/novelty and commitment often correlate with stronger comedic payoff; lower scores for predictable, safe choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity is essential
rubrics_metrics.description: "I’ve only ever been disappointed when I wasn’t authentic" (Jim Carrey).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even in wildly animated characters, performances must be grounded in a truthful impulse. Anti-pattern: reaching for bits that feel manufactured or not emotionally honest; Carrey describes feeling he 'raped' himself when not authentic. Guidance: aim for emotional truth, not just surface gags.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use your whole instrument — energy and physicality
rubrics_metrics.description: "I love actors who employ every bit of their instrument"; extensive physical commitment and energy are praised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-energy physical choices (hoisting on tables, crawling through audience, intense facial/physical expression) create memorable comedy. Example: Carrey's stage war, crawling behind piano, improvised physical bits. Low-energy or minimal commitment may undercut jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel personal life and trauma into material ('calomedy')
rubrics_metrics.description: Carrey describes his show as 'calomedy' — calamity handled with humor; performers use personal trauma/emotion in their work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use real-life pain, anger, disappointment as creative material to generate depth (tragicomedy). Example: converting life hardships into characters or themes. Anti-pattern: treating trauma superficially or only for shock without emotional payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know techniques but adapt them for you
rubrics_metrics.description: Carrey: knows Stanislavsky, Meisner, and uses what’s good for him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be literate in acting methods but be pragmatic: adopt elements that serve your performance rather than slavishly following a single technique. Guidance: study methods to expand tools; apply selectively based on role and personal process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure scenes: setup, joke, and an out
rubrics_metrics.description: Sacha Baron Cohen: "know the setup to the joke, the joke, and I need an out."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Especially in risky or hidden-camera work, clearly plan the scene’s beats and an exit strategy. Scoring: clarity of setup and reliable exit increases safety and preserves the bit. Anti-pattern: entering improvisation without an exit, increasing danger and reducing control.

rubrics_metrics.name: In hidden-camera/immersion comedy, never 'crack' or reveal character
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohen: if it’s going to get violent, the worst thing is to crack and have them realize you’re playing a character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain character under threat; breaking character destroys the scene and can escalate danger. Example: Cohen rehearses interrogation techniques and edits scenes mentally to avoid exposure. Safety contingency planning is critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk assessment and mitigation for dangerous/prank work
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel emphasizes calculating probabilities of bad outcomes and preparing contingencies (back rooms, fake IDs, ex-Secret Service, opting-in crew).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before stunts/pranks, assess legal/physical risks and implement mitigations: trained backup (security), alternate exit rooms, legal counsel, crew consent/opt-in, acting-as-producer to manage safety. Anti-pattern: ad hoc setups without contingency or crew buy-in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared to act as producer / take responsibility for safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohen: at times you have to 'act as the producer' and tell crew to opt in to next scene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performers in risky shoots should step into a production role to manage consent and safety, confirming everyone understands risks for subsequent takes. Practical steps: explicit crew check-ins, pause when danger increases, clear rules for continuing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative boundary-setting on sensitive material
rubrics_metrics.description: Don Cheadle: showrunners may push jokes; he sometimes reins them in and suggests alternatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams must negotiate ethical/ethical-sensitivity lines (e.g., anti-Semitic or racist jokes). Use collaborative judgment to redirect humor rather than blindly repeating harmful tropes. Anti-pattern: accepting offensive material without considering impact or alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence and resilience in front of hostile audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Carrey recounts staying on stage for two hours while the audience hated him; persistence can convert hostility into breakthrough moments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Live performance may meet hostility; resilience, endurance, and the willingness to escalate or change approach can salvage a set. Anti-pattern: quitting too early or abandoning a risky bit at the first hostile response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid typecasting by choosing varied or challenging roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Panelists note Hollywood 'locks people in lanes' and discuss turning down repetitive/weak versions of roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To avoid being pigeonholed, decline scripts that are merely variations of previous parts; seek roles that expand range (tragicomedy, dramatic turns). Practical: evaluate offers for novelty and depth; say no to lazy duplicates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host the audience’s opinion graciously
rubrics_metrics.description: Ted Danson: 'you still have to host their opinion of you graciously.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when criticized or misperceived, respond with professionalism rather than denial or hostility. This maintains public relationships and career stability. Anti-pattern: publicly fighting audience perceptions aggressively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use vulnerability wisely — let go of created personas
rubrics_metrics.description: Carrey: people create your life; to go forward you must let go of the created persona.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actors should recognize the persona constructed by fame and intentionally release it to preserve sanity and creative freedom. Practical advice: protect private life, set boundaries around publicity, and avoid sustaining an inauthentic public mask.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for emotional transitions (tragicomedy) to engage audiences deeply
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohen and others praise tragicomedy: characters who are funny then experience tragedy, transitioning audience sympathy rapidly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek projects or create material where comedic attachment leads to emotional investment; the pivot from laughter to sadness can be powerful. Anti-pattern: flat jokes without stakes or emotional payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Know your limits with substance/physical approximations on screen
rubrics_metrics.description: Panel mentions using B12 or other methods to approximate a high and concerns about tolerance and call times.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful of methods used to simulate states (e.g., being 'high') — prioritize health, legal/production rules, and reliability of performance. Anti-pattern: unsafe reliance on substances or unhealthy practices to achieve a state.
